The bull case runs on the third fiscal quarter ended 2026-07-31, when revenue of $1.85 billion rose 36.54% from a year earlier, net income of $397 million rose 107.85%, gross margin was 65.87%, net margin was 21.51% and earnings per share of 2.82 exceeded the 2.16 estimate by 30.56% [D1]. The strength was broad, with Communications Solutions Group revenue of $1.35 billion up 43.09% and operating income of $458 million up 86.18%, Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue of $501 million up 21.6% and operating income of $155 million up 68.48%, and total segment operating income of $613 million up 81.36% [D1]. Guidance for the fourth fiscal quarter is revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion, which at the mid-point is 37% growth, and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 on a diluted share count of 172 million [D1]. What the bull case needs from the next report is revenue inside that $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion range and earnings per share inside 3.34 to 3.40, with the segment operating momentum of the third quarter still intact [D1].

The bear case starts with the market's verdict on the same quarter, since the move in the session after the 2026-08-18 release, on 2026-08-19, was -6.32% despite the 30.56% earnings surprise [D1]. It then takes management at its word that the binding constraint is supply rather than demand, with the supply environment described as less flexible than a year earlier and supply expected to remain the governor of near-term revenue for the next several quarters [D3]. The quarter also carried one-time tariff impacts that management said artificially pulled up fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat, which raises the bar for the next comparison [D3]. On the reported numbers, the sequential step was modest, with revenue up 7.51% on the quarter before [D1]. What the bear case needs from the next report is revenue at or below the low end of the $1.93 billion guidance or earnings per share at or below 3.34 [D1]. It also needs confirmation that component supply is capping conversion of a demand pipeline that management says is still growing strongly [D3].
